name: Kiribati

findings.local_actor: Government of Kiribati (East Micronesia Cable partner)
findings.reversal_of: HMN Tech low bid in the World Bank/ADB-backed East Micronesia Cable tender (Kiribati, Nauru, FSM)
findings.summary: The US$72.6m World Bank-led East Micronesia Cable tender, where HMN Tech bid over 20% below ASN and NEC, ended without award after US security warnings over the Guam-linked HANTRU1 connection; all bids were deemed non-compliant.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 2: a lowest bid in an open tender, never a signed contract. All three 2021 outcome reports derive from one Reuters scoop, so not coded as independently corroborated; DCD (Dec 2020) independently covers the US warning only. US$72.6m is project value, not HMN's bid, so values left null. still_current true because the cable was later rebuilt by NEC (KIR-002). Capacity article date not shown on page.

findings.financier: Governments of Australia, Japan and the United States (grants)
findings.summary: NEC built the 2,250 km East Micronesia Cable System linking Tarawa to Nauru and FSM, Tarawa's first submarine cable, co-owned by state-owned BNL and grant-funded by Australia, Japan and the US; NEC announced completion in May 2026.
findings.analyst_inference: Cable equipment vendor NEC (Japan), so pole third despite US co-funding. Tier 4: construction completed per May 2026 report; ready-for-service in Kiribati not confirmed in opened sources. US$95m is DCD's conversion of the AUD 135m total three-country project estimate, not a Kiribati-only figure. Effectively replaces the HMN bid (KIR-001).

findings.summary: Kiribati's telecom regulator announced Starlink had launched internet service in the country and dropped apparatus licensing for Starlink users, while still requiring type approval of imported terminals.
findings.analyst_inference: Both sources are the same regulator, so not corroborated; single opened S1 permits medium. Tier 4 as regulatory authorisation plus service launch; subscriber scale unknown, so not tier 5.
